lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, the promise could not be recorded because of a technical problem.

lines.dispute_line: I understand, and I won't go into it further on this call.

lines.restructure_line: I'll connect you with our restructuring team, who can discuss repayment options with you.
lines.human_ask_help: Is there anything I can help you with myself?

lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, a promise cannot be changed on this call.

lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I did not catch that. Do you confirm, yes or no?
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {amount}.

quotes: A skipped step is not a proposal and does not count towards the limit; go straight to the next step.
This opening question does not count towards the product's persuasion limit; the limit counts only the ladder steps of F.2.
For F.3, however, the opening question is treated like a proposal already made: a ladder step identical to it is skipped.

rules.too_much_skips_full.assumption: Once the customer says the full amount is too much, the next proposal is the floor (E.2); nothing is said about skipping later full-amount steps, so the default applies.

quotes: "That is too much" means the next proposal you make is the floor.
1. the full overdue amount on the deadline;
rules.too_much_floor.derivation: The opening question is not a proposal; the next proposal is ladder step 1 (on the deadline) and counts towards the limit, so the floor replaces attempt 1 on attempt 1's date.

quotes: Stop proposing when the product's persuasion limit is reached or the ladder has no steps left, whichever comes first.
Each flat refusal (a no with no date and no amount) moves to the next step of the ladder:
rules.refuse_deadline_is_refusal.derivation: Saying no to a proposal on the deadline with no other date or amount is a flat refusal and moves to the next step.

quotes: If `create_promise` fails twice, note `service_error` on that product.
rules.promise_retries.derivation: service_error only comes after the second failure, so a failed create_promise is retried once.

quotes: Financial hardship (job loss, illness, bereavement): one sentence of sympathy, make no proposals, note `hardship` on each remaining product and close `no_promise` / `hardship`.
rules.hardship_transfer.derivation: Sympathy only, nothing is offered and nobody is transferred. 'direct' with an empty support queue gives sympathy and then the hardship close, without asking a question.

quotes: Only then, if the date you have is not a business day, move it forward to the next business day.
A customer who names a non-business day on or before the deadline is offered the next business day; a date after the deadline is answered with the deadline.
rules.deadline_adjust.derivation: Non-business dates move forward to the next business day.

quotes: For each product, the first thing the agent asks is: "Can you pay the full overdue amount of EUR {amount} today?"

rules.week_end_today.assumption: The ladder has no end-of-week steps, so this does not apply.

products.floor_min.assumption: There is no minimum floor beyond the overdraft rule for debts under 100.

overdraft: one quarter of `overdue_eur`, rounded up to the next whole euro (a whole-euro result stays as it is).
half the overdue amount, rounded up to the next whole euro (a whole-euro result stays), on the deadline; if that is below the floor, the floor instead;
`create_promise` takes the amount in euro cents, as a whole number (EUR 45.10 is 4510).

quotes: For calls made on or after 4 November 2026, the `close_call` reason `hardship` is replaced by `financial_difficulty` (outcome stays `no_promise`).

assumptions: Verification ends after 2 wrong answers in total (C.2: 'The second wrong answer, counted across both questions, ends verification'). This is the bank's more specific rule and overrides the API summary of three.
The order of security questions follows C.1: phone_last4 first, then date_of_birth.
date_order is dmy because C.1 says a spoken all-numeric date is read day, month, year. The answer is sent as YYYY-MM-DD.

Tier 2 deadline: the 15th of this month, rolled to next month's 15th only if it is before today (so on the 15th the deadline is today). The roll happens before the date is moved forward to the next business day (D.3 'Only then').
deadline_adjust is next_business_day from D.3 and D.4. Tier 1 deadlines are always business days already.
Ladder step 2 = 50% of the overdue amount, rounded up to the whole euro (whole results stay), then max(that, floor). The engine clamps a percentage step to the floor.

Overdraft floor = 25% of overdue_eur, rounded up to the whole euro. If overdue_eur < 100 the floor is the full overdue amount. A floor is never above the amount owed. Examples: 99.50 -> 99.50; 100 -> 25; 101 -> 25.25 -> 26.

Persuasion limits (2 for Tier 1, 3 for Tier 2) count only ladder steps. The opening 'full amount today' question is not counted, but it blocks an identical step. Example: a Tier 2 deadline of today makes step 1 (full on the deadline) identical to the opening, so it is skipped and not counted.
'That is too much' makes the next proposal the floor. That proposal is attempt 1 on the deadline (too_much_floor attempt_1).
Brief B.1 prescribes 'This call is recorded.'; the format requires active voice, so the opening says 'We record this call.'
The brief's prescribed opening ask 'Can you pay the full overdue amount of EUR {amount} today?' is written without the literal 'EUR' because {amount} already includes the currency.
The brief has no title variable, so confirm_ask uses {first_name} {last_name} as B.1 says.

Hardship: there is no support transfer in this brief. Sympathy, no proposals, hardship notes on the remaining products, close no_promise/hardship. transfer_support has no queue and mirrors the hardship close.
Memo OPS-26-31: from 2026-11-04 the hardship close reason is financial_difficulty. Before that date it is hardship. add_note reason hardship is unchanged.
Products outside 1-60 days: the brief gives no rule, so bands_outside is not set.
The callback must be today or the next business day, 09:30-18:00 inclusive, later than now, with 2 tries. The brief does not require today to be a business day.
next_weekday interpretation is not stated; default following_week.
max_not_talk is not stated; default 2.
Asking 'anything else' after a recorded promise is not stated; the default is kept.
Changing a recorded promise is not covered; the agent says it cannot be changed on this call.
A failed create_promise is retried once (F.5 'fails twice'), then service_error is noted on that product.
No discounts, waivers, fee reversals or payment plans are offered (F.6). The agent's lines never offer them.
Below-floor offers: the floor is offered once, and a refusal of it is treated as a refusal (E.2). The word 'recorded' is kept out of these lines, so they say 'can't accept'.
The queue code table comes from the transfer_to_agent enum in the API. The brief only uses restructuring and general.
